verdict.rationale: cubic's privacy docs say its AI model providers (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic) contractually commit not to use customer code snippets or metadata passed through their APIs for training, so the core no-training protection is in place by default. The documented commitment covers only third-party providers, though, and the only user-side control documented is asking to block AI features entirely. Missing for 10: an explicit statement on whether cubic itself trains on customer data, a documented user-facing training opt-out setting, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can prevent my data from being used to train AI models

citations.quote: Our AI model providers (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic) contractually commit that code snippets and metadata passed through their APIs are not used to train or improve their underlying models.
